FINAL ANSWER (per approved design; raw mean of the supplied BatchCorrectedReadCounts is the headline):

Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and mean expression across the 132 CD14 samples, for the 19,942 protein-coding genes (exact gene_biotype == 'protein_coding'), is r ≈ 0.03 (0.0317) — essentially no linear association.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT (transform sensitivity, as you requested): the three variants differ substantially. Raw mean r = 0.0317; CPM-normalized mean r = 0.0293 (depth normalization barely changes it); but log2(mean CPM + 1) gives r = 0.2699. The raw mean distribution is extremely right-skewed (skew 40.6, max 354,289), so Pearson on the raw scale is dominated by a few very highly expressed genes; a log transform reveals a modest positive length–expression association (~0.27). So: the headline literal reading gives ~0.03 (no correlation), but the result is transform-sensitive — on the log scale there is a weak-to-moderate positive correlation. The CPM-vs-raw agreement shows library-size depth is NOT the driver of the difference; the log compression is.

Full variant table:
- PRIMARY: raw mean, all 19,942 PC genes (incl. 1,849 all-zero): r = 0.0317
- Variant A: CPM-normalized mean, all PC genes: r = 0.0293
- Variant B: log2(mean CPM + 1), all PC genes: r = 0.2699
- Sens. 1 (exclude 1,849 all-zero genes, raw mean): r = 0.0223 (with-vs-without difference is negligible: 0.0317 → 0.0223)
- Sens. 2 (incl. the 12 mixed-biotype protein_coding-token rows): r = 0.0317 (unchanged to 4 dp); with all-zero excluded: r = 0.0222
So the biotype-quirk and all-zero-gene decisions have negligible impact; the transform choice is the only consequential one.

Execution details (all invariants verified at runtime):
- Join invariants OK: 59,453 gene IDs identical across meta and counts; 723 sample IDs identical across counts columns and annotation rows; 0 missing values anywhere; all Length > 0.
- CD14 subset: 132 samples via celltype == 'CD14' (authoritative mapping; only 118 IDs end in literal 'CD14', 14 have _1/_2 suffixes — the suffix trap was avoided). CD14 matrix 59,453 × 132, total counts 1,837,874,885.
- Pearson computed on n = 19,942 (Length, mean-expression) gene pairs; no TPM/gene-length normalization of expression, no low-expression filtering, Spearman not used.

Deliverable: executed script analysis/pearson_length_expr_cd14.py (with runtime invariant assertions) and printed/written summary analysis/results_summary.txt.
